# Blend

> Blend is a dotfile manager for macOS and Linux. Configuration is composed in Nickel, rendered to the files applications read, compared with those files by meaning, and reconciled in either direction.

Blend works with two views of a configuration. The Source is a checkout of `orders/<name>/order.ncl` files; the Target is the deployed file an application reads. `blend view` explains differences without writing, and `blend sync` reconciles them: Source to Target rewrites the deployed file, while Target to Source carries an application's edit back into the Nickel declaration where a concrete value can be rewritten safely. Ownership policies in the Order can settle recurring differences automatically. Structured output covers TOML, JSON, JSONC, YAML, plaintext, and simple `key value` / `key=value` line formats.

## Docs

- [User guide](https://blend.pyonpyon.today/guide/): Orders, Nickel composition, formats, inspecting, reconciling, and safety boundaries
- [User guide (Markdown)](https://blend.pyonpyon.today/guide.md): the same guide as raw Markdown, from docs/GUIDE.md in the repository
- [README](https://github.com/frantic1048/blend/blob/main/README.md): overview, installation, and a first example

## Project

- [Homepage](https://blend.pyonpyon.today/): an introduction with worked examples
- [Source repository](https://github.com/frantic1048/blend): code, issues, and the canonical documentation
- [Releases](https://github.com/frantic1048/blend/releases): prebuilt archives for Apple silicon macOS, Intel macOS, and ARM64 or x86-64 GNU/Linux, plus the release installer and multi-architecture GHCR image
